metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: when you ask Claude to turn a resolved ticket into a knowledge base article, is it deciding on its own that the moment calls for one — or checking a written file first? Lands the carry-out that Claude checks the same written triggers on any input, and what it covers is exactly what that file names.

beats.narration_text: Someone wondered if Claude just senses when a ticket is worth writing up. It doesn't — it checks a written skill file. So: can Claude draft a knowledge base article using a skill file?

TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('instinct' -> 'a skill file') lands on screen and the full corrected question finishes typing before the clip ends. Timing rates (charMs=42, mistakeRate=4%, hesitateWithin=2%, hesitateBetween=8%, jitter=26) are the calibrated values proven on the `agent-development`, `close-month`, and `journal-entry-prep` siblings, applied here from the start.

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it acts. This one is called kb-article, and its SKILL.md file is the instruction set — plain language, no hidden logic. Claude reads the file, then follows it. The file is the whole program.

The instructions run as a pipeline. Read the SKILL.md file and load the instruction set. Execute each step in order. Return the finished article as the result. Linear — no branching unless a step says so.

production_viz.label: THE STEPS
production_viz.caption: steps run in order, not by feel

beats.narration_text: Run it on the same resolved ticket twice and you get the same article both times — same input, same output. That covers what the file names: a ticket worth documenting, a recurring question, a workaround to publish, or a known issue to communicate. Anything the file doesn't name, it doesn't do.

production_viz.label: RELIABLE, AND ONLY THAT WIDE
production_viz.caption: reliable, and no wider than the file names

beats.narration_text: Claude doesn't decide a ticket deserves a knowledge base article because it feels that way — it checks the same written triggers every time. What it covers is exactly what that file names, and nothing past it.

props.quote: Claude doesn't decide a ticket deserves a knowledge base article because it feels that way — it checks the same written triggers every time. What it covers is exactly what that file names, and nothing past it.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I have a resolved support ticket — or a question customers keep asking. I want to draft a knowledge base article from it. Read the kb-article skill first, and walk me through what you'll do before you do it. That last part matters — asking Claude to explain itself first is how you catch a bad step before it runs.
